Smoothness of an integer

Source: R/ntheory.R
smoothness.Rd

smoothness(n) returns c(B, Bpow): the largest prime factor of n and the largest prime power dividing it. smoothness_p(n, m, power, visual) reports the smoothness of p + m for every prime power p^i in n, sorted by B (power = 0) or Bpow (power = 1). It returns list(m, entries) where each entry is c(p, i, B, Bpow); with visual = TRUE it returns the report as a string, which it also accepts back as input.

Usage

smoothness(n)

smoothness_p(n, m = -1, power = 0, visual = NULL)

Arguments

n

An integer, a factor vector, a report string or a returned list.

m

Offset added to each prime.

power

0 or 1, the sort key.

visual

TRUE for the string report, FALSE for the list.

Value

As described above.

Examples

smoothness(2^7 * 3^2)
#> [1]   3 128
smoothness_p(10431, m = 1)
#> [[1]]
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [[2]][[1]]
#> [1] 3 2 2 4
#> 
#> [[2]][[2]]
#> [1] 19  1  5  5
#> 
#> [[2]][[3]]
#> [1] 61  1 31 31
#> 
#> 
cat(smoothness_p(10431, m = 1, visual = TRUE))
#> p**i=3**2 has p+1 B=2, B-pow=4
#> p**i=19**1 has p+1 B=5, B-pow=5
#> p**i=61**1 has p+1 B=31, B-pow=31
